title: Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification
description: Used to provide a correct Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) to the person who is required to file an information return with the IRS to report certain transactions.
summary: This is the form you fill out when someone needs your Social Security Number or Employer ID Number for tax reporting — for example, when you start a new job, open a bank account, or do freelance work. You do not send this form to the IRS. You give it to the business or person who requested it.

title: Employee's Withholding Certificate
description: Completed by employees to let their employer know how much federal income tax to withhold from their pay.
summary: You fill out this form when you start a new job or when you want to change how much tax is taken out of your paycheck. Your employer uses it to calculate your tax withholding. The IRS website has a withholding estimator tool to help you fill it out.

title: Application for Employer Identification Number
description: Used to apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS for a business entity.
summary: This form is used to get an EIN — a tax ID number for a business. You need an EIN if you are starting a business, hiring employees, opening a business bank account, or forming a partnership or corporation. You can also apply for an EIN online through the IRS website.

title: U.S. Individual Income Tax Return
description: The standard IRS form used by individuals to file their annual income tax return.
summary: This is the main form used to file your federal income taxes each year. Most people use this form to report their income, claim deductions and credits, and calculate what they owe or what refund they will receive.

title: Ohio BMV Power of Attorney for Certificate of Title
description: Allows a vehicle owner to authorize another person to sign title paperwork and handle BMV title transactions on their behalf.
summary: This form lets you give someone else permission to sign title paperwork and handle BMV transactions for your vehicle. People commonly use this when they cannot go to the BMV in person or when a title agency is handling a vehicle sale.

title: Ohio BMV Application for Certificate of Title to a Motor Vehicle
description: Application for an Ohio certificate of title. Used for obtaining a new title, duplicate title, or transfer of title.
summary: This is the main form used to apply for an Ohio vehicle certificate of title. Use it when you buy a vehicle, lose your title and need a replacement marked "DUPLICATE," or transfer ownership. There is a fee. You will need to provide identification and proof of ownership.

title: Ohio BMV Ownership Assignment and Title Application for Casual Sale
description: Title application and ownership assignment for a casual (private party) sale of a motor vehicle in Ohio.
summary: This form is used when you buy or sell a vehicle through a private sale (not from a dealership) in Ohio. It serves as both the title application and the ownership assignment. The seller signs over the title and the buyer applies for a new title in their name.

title: Ohio BMV Affidavit for Designation of Beneficiary for Certificate of Title
description: Allows the sole owner of a motor vehicle, watercraft, or outboard motor to designate a beneficiary to receive the title upon the owner's death.
summary: If you are the sole owner of a vehicle in Ohio, this form lets you name someone who will automatically receive the vehicle title when you pass away. This can help avoid probate for your vehicle. The form must be filed with the county title office.

title: Ohio Application for Notary Public Commission
description: Resources and FAQ for becoming a notary public in Ohio, including requirements, application process, and background check information.
summary: This is a resource page from the Ohio Secretary of State with frequently asked questions about becoming a notary public. It covers the application process, background check requirements, educational requirements, and how to renew your commission. Notaries in Ohio are commissioned for five-year terms.

title: Hamilton County Auditor Forms Directory
description: Directory of downloadable PDF forms from the Hamilton County Auditor's Office, including conveyance forms, tax exemption applications, dog licensing, and CAUV forms.
summary: The Hamilton County Auditor's forms page includes downloadable forms for real estate transfers, tax exemptions, dog licensing, agricultural use valuation, name change affidavits, and other property-related filings. This is the central page for finding county-level property forms.

title: Hamilton County Vital Records Requests
description: Vital records services from Hamilton County Public Health, including birth and death certificate requests.
summary: Hamilton County Public Health provides certified copies of birth and death certificates for events that occurred in Hamilton County, Ohio. Certified copies are often needed for identification, passports, school registration, estate settlement, and insurance claims. Fees apply and proof of identity is required.

title: Application for a Social Security Card
description: Used to apply for an original Social Security card, request a replacement, or update information on your Social Security record. All forms are free.
summary: Use this form to get a new Social Security card, replace a lost card, or update your name on your Social Security record. You will need to provide documents proving your identity, age, and citizenship or immigration status. The Social Security Administration does not charge for a Social Security card. Available in English and Spanish.

title: Application for Retirement Insurance Benefits
description: Application for Social Security retirement insurance benefits. Available in English and Spanish.
summary: This is the form used to apply for Social Security retirement benefits. The SSA also allows you to apply online through their website, but this paper form is available for those who need it or prefer it. You can apply up to four months before you want your benefits to start.

title: Application for Disability Insurance Benefits
description: Application for Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits. Available in English and Spanish.
summary: If you cannot work because of a medical condition expected to last at least one year or result in death, you may use this form to apply for SSDI benefits. Most people apply online or by phone, but the paper form is available if needed.

title: Authorization to Disclose Information to the Social Security Administration
description: Authorizes medical sources, schools, and other parties to disclose information to the SSA for claims processing.
summary: This form lets the SSA request your medical records and other personal information when you apply for benefits like Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income. By signing it, you give healthcare providers and other sources permission to share your information with the SSA. Includes instructions in English and Spanish.
